assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced degradation of proteins through the ubiquitin-proteasome system, via heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, is a new therapeutic modality with a clear chemical logic. It also links to the cellular proteostasis and regulated-turnover machinery I know from RNR and dNTP-pool control, where regulated protein degradation is central.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies made the founding PROTAC concept and first demonstration (2001); Ciulli's VHL-ligand-based work made the approach drug-like. The thalidomide-cereblon discovery (Handa, Ito) is a distinct molecular-glue strand that the three-name limit leaves out, so credit is a real tension.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials and the mechanism has been confirmed independently in many laboratories. Recognition is timely, although approved PROTAC drugs are still few.
uncertainties: Whether the glue/CRBN strand (Handa, Gray) must be recognized with PROTACs given the three-laureate cap.
I have not verified current clinical approval status; I recall it only from general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks, by engineering deaminases onto Cas9 nickases. This is a chemistry-driven tool that changes DNA at single-nucleotide resolution, with direct relevance to genome stability and mutagenesis, and it has therapeutic use.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory, with Komor and Gaudelli as the lead inventors, made the decisive contribution. Liu alone is a defensible single-laureate choice, but the inventors' credit and the question of whether the prize belongs in Chemistry rather than Medicine are open. CRISPR itself was recognized in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Independent replication is extensive and the first clinical base-editing results are appearing. Recognition is timely, though the clinical evidence is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the junior inventors should share credit.
Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize may count against it.
Exact clinical-validation status not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators made DNA sequencing cheap and massively parallel, and it underpins mutation-signature, replication-fidelity and cancer-genome work in my own field. Its impact on biology and medicine has been transformative.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry. Rothberg (pyrosequencing and 454), Mayer (Lynx) and Ju (reversible terminators) are other strands, so the attribution is contested and the field is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly validated; this is the dominant sequencing technology of the last two decades. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Contested priority among parallel sequencing platforms.
Frame is analytical chemistry, but the committee may see it as closer to Medicine or Physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25% in little more than a decade, a remarkable materials-chemistry story. It is far from my own area, so I rely on the general record.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell (2009); Park made the first solid-state cell (2012); Snaith made the planar and mixed-halide advances. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are also strong claimants, so a three-person selection is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are reproduced widely, but long-term stability and commercial deployment are unresolved, so the case may be slightly premature.
uncertainties: Who among Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis should be dropped is a hard allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal that phase separation organizes membraneless compartments in cells reframed cell biology and relates directly to the physical chemistry of biomolecular condensates. It is conceptually original and widely influential.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids (2009); Rosen showed multivalent interactions drive phase separation (2012). Pappu and Mittag supply key physical theory and are not credited in this selection.
assessment.maturity: The field is young and debated, in particular whether condensates in vivo are functionally driven by phase separation. Mature enough to be considered, but possibly premature.
uncertainties: Ongoing debate about the in vivo physiological relevance of liquid-liquid phase separation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made siRNA and mRNA medicines deliverable, and they enabled the COVID-19 vaccines and Onpattro. The impact is large and concrete, in lipid and pharmaceutical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues established the ionizable lipid LNP systems; Anderson and Langer developed combinatorial lipid libraries and delivery methods. MacLachlan, Hope and Madden also contributed. The six-name list is hard to reduce, and the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA already touched this area.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale; very mature. The proximity to the 2023 Medicine prize is a timing concern.
uncertainties: Complicated credit among many contributors and companies.
Possible redundancy with the 2023 Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics made quantitative, proteome-wide measurement of proteins possible. I use LC-MS/MS myself in nucleotide-pool measurement, so I know its power. The soft-ionization advance already received the 2002 prize.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution and SILAC-type proteomics), Aebersold (targeted and quantitative proteomics) and Yates (shotgun and MudPIT) are the main leaders; Hunt, Gygi and Heck are other plausible claimants.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and broadly adopted. The earlier prize for ionization methods and the many claimants reduce the likelihood of a focused award.
uncertainties: Crowded credit across many method developers.
May look incremental after the 2002 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic-code expansion, by orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs encoding unnatural amino acids, gives chemists site-specific control of proteins in living cells. It is original, general and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang made the first in vivo demonstration; Chin extended it to eukaryotes and to quadruple codons and recoded genomes. Mehl and Yokoyama are further claimants.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and used extensively, though broad therapeutic uptake is still limited; timely.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among five names.
